scope: read-only sampling of existing versioned fixture baselines and their seed/scan tooling

reviewed.finding: Useful synthetic subject and runtime-gate conventions, but it does not provide the six P1R categories or cleanup ownership.
Useful owner-service and deterministic seed conventions, but it is coupled to B25 schemas and does not provide order/privacy request fixtures.
Useful synthetic reference policy and raw-media prohibition; retained as historical staging evidence.
Useful content snapshot, replay, and privacy projection conventions; retained as a task-specific historical fixture.
Useful owner-chain and no-raw-payload conventions, but it is not a seedable data set.
Contains deliberately synthetic but email- and phone-shaped values for security tests; these values were not copied into the P1R baseline.
Provides guarded database replay/purge ideas, but has live MySQL mode and local credential defaults; the P1R M0 tool never imports or executes it.
Provides useful sensitive-field and destructive-SQL checks; P1R applies stricter reserved-reference, audio-metadata-only, sandbox-order, and ownership-marker checks.
Provides useful non-synthetic domain scanning; P1R validation is self-contained and does not depend on business packages.

decision.reason: Existing fixtures are fragmented by historical batch, schema, or test purpose and cannot form a standalone P1R seed/cleanup contract without inheriting legacy coupling.
